syllabus.source: Engineering Studies Stage 6 Syllabus (Amended 2011), Board of Studies NSW
syllabus.purpose: Syllabus keyword database for CUBE Marking Coach — HSC module content only. Keywords are strictly from NESA syllabus text.
hsc_outcomes: H1.1 describes the scope of engineering and critically analyses current innovations
H1.2 differentiates between the properties and structure of materials and justifies the selection of materials in engineering applications
H2.1 determines suitable properties, uses and applications of materials, components and processes in engineering
H2.2 analyses and synthesises engineering applications in specific fields and reports on the importance of these to society
H3.1 demonstrates proficiency in the use of mathematical, scientific and graphical methods to analyse and solve problems of engineering practice
H3.2 uses appropriate written, oral and presentation skills in the preparation of detailed engineering reports
H3.3 develops and uses specialised techniques in the application of graphics as a communication tool
H4.1 investigates the extent of technological change in engineering
H4.2 applies knowledge of history and technological change to engineering-based problems
H4.3 applies understanding of social, environmental and cultural implications of technological change in engineering to the analysis of specific engineering problems
H5.1 works individually and in teams to solve specific engineering problems and prepare engineering reports
H5.2 selects and uses appropriate management and planning skills related to engineering
H6.1 demonstrates skills in research and problem-solving related to engineering
H6.2 demonstrates skills in analysis, synthesis and experimentation related to engineering

cube_app_usage_notes.keyword_principle: All keywords are strictly from NESA syllabus text only. Students may be examined on any syllabus keyword. Content beyond the syllabus (e.g. specific named examples of structures, aircraft, or systems) will be provided as stimulus material in the exam.
cube_app_usage_notes.topic_structure: Four HSC modules: two engineering application modules (Civil Structures, Personal and Public Transport) and two engineering focus modules (Aeronautical Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering). Students complete one Engineering Report from either application module and one from either focus module.
cube_app_usage_notes.subtopic_codes: CS = Civil Structures, PPT = Personal and Public Transport, AE = Aeronautical Engineering, TE = Telecommunications Engineering

bandRules.purpose: Band descriptor rules for generating indicative HSC responses at each band level. Used by CUBE Marking Coach model answer generator.
bandRules.source_basis: NESA Engineering Studies 2025 Course Report band descriptors (verbatim). Engineering Studies Stage 6 Syllabus (Amended 2011).

always: Align all content to the NSW HSC Engineering Studies syllabus.
Answer the directive verb exactly as asked.
Use accurate engineering terminology, methods and conventions throughout.
Keep all claims relevant to the question and the engineering context.
Use graphical and analytical methods where appropriate to the question.
Apply cause-and-effect reasoning when explaining engineering principles.
Reference relevant materials, structures, properties, processes or mechanics concepts as required by the question.

identify: Name the required feature, process, material, component or engineering concept.
Do not explain unless the question demands it.
outline: Provide the main features or general steps.
describe: State relevant characteristics, features and what they do or show.
Include structure, function or behaviour where appropriate.
explain: Show cause and effect clearly using engineering reasoning.
Link ideas using explicit technical connections.
analyse: Break the concept or problem into parts.
Show relationships, causes, effects or patterns using engineering evidence.
assess: Make a judgement based on strengths and limitations.
Support the judgement with engineering evidence or data.
evaluate: Judge the overall value, effectiveness or significance.
Include strengths, limitations and a clear final judgement.
justify: Give engineering reasons that support a conclusion or choice.
compare: Show similarities and differences between the engineering concepts, materials or processes.
contrast: Focus on differences between the engineering concepts, materials or processes.
recommend: Propose a course of action or solution with engineering justification.
Link the recommendation to the engineering context.
calculate: Show all working including formula, substitution of values and units.
State the final answer with correct units and appropriate significant figures.
construct: Produce the required diagram, drawing or graphical solution.
Apply appropriate Australian Standard (AS 1100) conventions where relevant.
trace: Follow the development or history of a component, process or concept over time.
Link changes to engineering innovation and societal impact.

Band6.nesa_descriptor: Demonstrates extensive knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices. Constructs and evaluates engineering reports in order to recommend and predict solutions. Chooses, performs and evaluates graphical and analytical solutions. Demonstrates an expertise in the analysis and solution of mechanics problems. Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of the structure and property relationship between materials and manufacturing processes by interpreting test results and explaining design limitations. Identifies materials and processes used in the past. Is critically aware of the social, cultural and historical issues in engineering. Demonstrates sophisticated written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using appropriate engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
Band6.knowledge_standard: Demonstrates extensive knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices.
Band6.communication_standard: Demonstrates sophisticated written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using appropriate engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
must_include: Extensive and precise engineering terminology used consistently throughout.
Engineering reports constructed and evaluated with clear recommendations and predictions.
Graphical and analytical solutions chosen, performed and evaluated — not just selected.
Expertise demonstrated in mechanics problem analysis and solution.
Comprehensive understanding of structure/property relationships linked to manufacturing processes, with test result interpretation and design limitations explained.
Materials and processes used historically identified and contextualised.
Critical awareness of social, cultural and historical issues in engineering.
Sophisticated written, graphical and mathematical communication applying correct engineering conventions.
style_rules: Communicate with sophistication — integrate multiple engineering concepts rather than listing facts.
Link materials science, mechanics, historical context and societal impact in extended responses.
Evaluate rather than merely describe — make explicit engineering judgements.
Apply correct engineering conventions (AS 1100, SI units, notation) consistently.
avoid: Generic statements without an engineering mechanism or data.
Describing without evaluating where the directive requires judgement.
Omitting units or using incorrect engineering conventions.
Word inflation without additional engineering depth.

short_response_2_3_marks: Directly answer the question in the first sentence using precise engineering terminology.
Include at least one explicit engineering link, mechanism or calculated value.
mid_response_4_6_marks: Include multiple linked engineering points across relevant topic areas.
Use evidence, examples, test data or calculations where applicable.
extended_response_7_plus_marks: Use a deliberate engineering structure addressing all parts of the question.
Sustain depth across mechanics, materials, communication and/or societal context.
Integrate evidence, terminology, graphical conventions and engineering judgement.
Address historical, social or cultural dimensions where relevant.

Band5.nesa_descriptor: Demonstrates thorough knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices. Assembles and organises information for engineering reports and makes recommendations and predictions based upon engineering reports. Chooses appropriate methods of graphical and analytical problem solving. Solves problems involving statics and dynamics by selecting and manipulating appropriate data into relevant formulae. Has a good understanding of manufacturing processes and the structure and property relationship between materials. Recognises the social, cultural and historical implications of technological change in engineering. Demonstrates highly developed written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using appropriate engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
Band5.knowledge_standard: Demonstrates thorough knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices.
Band5.communication_standard: Demonstrates highly developed written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using appropriate engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
must_include: Thorough engineering terminology used logically and effectively.
Information for engineering reports assembled and organised with recommendations and predictions made.
Appropriate graphical and analytical methods chosen for problem solving.
Statics and dynamics problems solved by selecting and manipulating appropriate data into relevant formulae.
Good understanding of manufacturing processes and structure/property relationships demonstrated.
Social, cultural and historical implications of technological change in engineering recognised.
Highly developed written, graphical and mathematical communication using appropriate engineering conventions.
style_rules: Communicate logically and effectively with thorough engineering detail.
Explain clearly with sound technical reasoning.
May be less integrated or less precisely expressed than Band 6 — some recommendations present but less comprehensive.
avoid: Significant errors in formulae, units or engineering conventions.
Ignoring the historical or societal dimension where the question requires it.

Band4.nesa_descriptor: Demonstrates sound knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices. Prepares and interprets engineering reports and makes some recommendations. Selects from both graphical and analytical solutions to solve problems. Has a working knowledge of the principles of engineering mechanics and can carry out relevant calculations to solve problems involving statics and dynamics. Links material structures with properties and therefore identifies appropriate manufacturing processes for a range of applications. Traces the development of selected components in engineering and their impact on society. Demonstrates sound written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using appropriate engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
Band4.knowledge_standard: Demonstrates sound knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices.
Band4.communication_standard: Demonstrates sound written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using appropriate engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
must_include: Sound engineering terminology used effectively.
Engineering reports prepared and interpreted with some recommendations made.
Both graphical and analytical solutions selected and applied.
Working knowledge of engineering mechanics principles with relevant calculations for statics and dynamics.
Material structures linked to properties, with appropriate manufacturing processes identified.
Development of selected engineering components traced with impact on society noted.
Sound written, graphical and mathematical communication using appropriate engineering conventions.
style_rules: Communicate clearly with sound engineering explanation.
Focus on correct core engineering ideas.
May be less detailed or less evaluative than Band 5 — some analysis present but limited depth.
avoid: Unsupported broad claims without engineering evidence.
Confusing or poorly sequenced engineering explanation.
Omitting relevant calculations or graphical solutions where required.

Band3.nesa_descriptor: Demonstrates basic knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices. Prepares and uses engineering reports. Processes data in problem-solving activities in engineering mechanics, such as by using forces, free body diagrams and vector geometry. Has a foundational understanding of manufacturing processes and the classification of materials. Demonstrates an awareness of the development and operation of engineered products and of the contribution of engineering to society. Demonstrates basic written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
Band3.knowledge_standard: Demonstrates basic knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices.
Band3.communication_standard: Demonstrates basic written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
must_include: Some correct engineering knowledge demonstrated.
Engineering reports prepared and used.
Data processed in problem-solving using forces, free body diagrams and vector geometry.
Foundational understanding of manufacturing processes and classification of materials.
Awareness of the development and operation of engineered products and engineering's contribution to society.
Basic written, graphical and mathematical communication using engineering terminology, methods and conventions.
style_rules: Communication is basic — limited depth and limited integration of engineering concepts.
avoid: Incorrect engineering science presented as fact.

Band2.nesa_descriptor: Demonstrates elementary knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices. Recognises the importance of engineering reports. Substitutes data into formulae while attempting to solve engineering mechanics problems. Interprets data from graphs, recalls basic definitions and identifies steps in manufacturing processes. Recognises that engineering processes impact upon people. Demonstrates elementary written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using simple engineering terminology and conventions.
Band2.knowledge_standard: Demonstrates elementary knowledge of the content, methodology, influences and responsibilities in engineering practices.
Band2.communication_standard: Demonstrates elementary written, graphical and mathematical communication skills, using simple engineering terminology and conventions.
must_include: Some isolated correct engineering ideas or basic definitions.
Recognition of the importance of engineering reports.
Data substituted into formulae while attempting to solve engineering mechanics problems.
Data interpreted from graphs; basic definitions recalled; steps in manufacturing processes identified.
Recognition that engineering processes impact upon people.
Elementary written, graphical and mathematical communication using simple engineering terminology and conventions.
style_rules: Communication is minimal — simple engineering terminology only.
avoid: Incorrect engineering formulae or invented science presented as fact.
Presenting a partial or incomplete answer as complete.

Band1.nesa_descriptor: Performance reported as Band 1 indicates that the minimum standard expected was not demonstrated.
Band1.knowledge_standard: Performance reported as Band 1 indicates that the minimum standard expected was not demonstrated.
Band1.communication_standard: Performance reported as Band 1 indicates that the minimum standard expected was not demonstrated.
must_include: No generation target. Used only as a fallback classification label for wholly inadequate responses.

identify.key_feature: Name only — no explanation required unless directed

outline.key_feature: Main features or steps — limited but accurate

explain.key_feature: Cause and effect with engineering reasoning

analyse.key_feature: Break into parts, show relationships and patterns

assess.key_feature: Judge strengths and limitations with evidence

evaluate.key_feature: Judge overall value or effectiveness with final judgement

justify.key_feature: Give engineering reasons supporting a conclusion

calculate.key_feature: Show formula, substitution, working, units, answer

trace.key_feature: Follow development over time, link to impact

Band6_explain: State the key engineering principle, process or concept precisely.
Explain the mechanism using correct engineering terminology.
Link cause to effect explicitly using engineering reasoning.
State the resulting consequence, significance or broader engineering impact.
Band6_analyse: Identify the major engineering components, forces or factors.
Show how they interact, relate or cause outcomes.
Interpret any trend, pattern, relationship or test data.
Link these relationships back to the engineering question.
Band6_evaluate: State the engineering solution, material, process or technology being evaluated.
Explain at least one strength with engineering evidence.
Explain at least one limitation with engineering evidence.
Make a clear final engineering judgement using 'overall', 'therefore' or 'this is effective because'.
Band6_assess: State the engineering issue and the criteria for judgement.
Discuss positive and negative aspects with engineering reasoning.
Use evidence, test data or calculated values.
Conclude with a balanced but definite engineering judgement.
Band6_describe: State the key engineering features, characteristics or components.
Explain what each feature does, shows or represents in engineering terms.
Use precise engineering terminology and conventions throughout.
Link features to their engineering function or significance where relevant.
Band6_outline: State the main engineering features or steps accurately.
Structure clearly if multiple features are required.
Band6_identify: Name the required engineering feature, process, material or concept directly.
Do not explain unless the question explicitly requires it.
If multiple items required, list clearly.
Band6_justify: State the engineering choice, solution or conclusion clearly.
Give engineering reasons supporting it with technical evidence.
Link each reason back to the engineering context.
Finish with a sentence confirming why the judgement is valid.
Band6_compare: Identify the engineering materials, processes or concepts being compared.
State similarities using precise engineering terminology.
Use comparative language (whereas, in contrast, similarly, unlike).
Band6_contrast: Identify the engineering materials, processes or concepts being contrasted.
Clearly state the key differences with engineering reasoning.
Use comparative language (whereas, in contrast, unlike).
Band6_recommend: State the recommended engineering solution, material or process clearly.
Give specific engineering reasons justifying the recommendation.
Address the engineering context and constraints.
Conclude with a statement confirming the recommendation is appropriate.
Band6_calculate: Substitute all values with correct SI units.
State the final answer with correct units and appropriate significant figures.
Band6_trace: Identify the starting point in the historical development of the engineering component or process.
Describe key stages of development using accurate engineering terminology.
Link changes to engineering innovation and improved performance.
Explain the impact on society, people or the environment.

before_output: Has the directive verb been answered correctly?
Has every part of the question been addressed?
Is the terminology appropriate to the target band?
Are engineering conventions (units, notation, AS 1100) applied correctly?
Have graphical or analytical methods been applied where relevant?
Has a judgement been made when required by the directive?
band6_checklist: Mechanisms explained and evaluated — not just stated.
Evidence, test data, calculations or historical context integrated.
Response is coherent and logically sequenced.
Judgement is explicit if required by the directive.

target_band_selection_rule.Band6: Generate with extensive precision — integrated engineering reasoning across mechanics, materials, historical context and societal impact. Evaluate rather than describe. Apply correct conventions throughout.
target_band_selection_rule.Band5: Generate with thorough, logically sound engineering explanation. Choose appropriate methods. Good understanding of materials and mechanics. Slightly less integrated or evaluative than Band 6.
target_band_selection_rule.Band4: Generate with sound core engineering content, effective terminology and some calculation or graphical work. Link materials to properties and manufacturing processes. Some recommendations present.
target_band_selection_rule.Band3: Generate basic, mostly descriptive responses using engineering terminology. Process data with forces and free body diagrams. Foundational understanding of materials and manufacturing.
target_band_selection_rule.Band2: Generate elementary responses — substitute data into formulae, interpret graphs, recall basic definitions. Recognise engineering's impact on society.
target_band_selection_rule.Band1: Do not intentionally generate unless explicitly requested as a wholly inadequate response example.

forbidden_behaviours: Do not generate Band 6 responses by merely increasing word count.
Do not add irrelevant advanced content to imitate sophistication.
Do not ignore the syllabus, engineering conventions or stimulus.
Do not use vague judgements such as 'it is good' without engineering criteria.
Do not omit units or engineering conventions in calculations or graphical work.
